messages.content: Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

**Subject: [Service Name] moves to [New Platform] on [Date]**

Hi [Name],

Next quarter we're moving [Service Name] onto [New Platform]. Your account, your data, and your billing all come with you — nothing to re-enter, nothing to re-approve.

Why now: the current system has been running on [old stack] since [year], and we've hit the ceiling on what we can add to it. [New Platform] gives us room for [specific capability, e.g. per-project permissions and an audit log], both of which customers have asked for repeatedly.

**What changes**

- Your sign-in address becomes [new URL] on [date]. The old address redirects for 12 months.
- API traffic should point at [new endpoint]. Existing keys keep working; the current endpoint stays live until [sunset date].
- [Feature X] works differently — see [link] for the specifics.

**What doesn't**

Pricing, contract terms, support hours, and your data retention settings are untouched.

**The cutover**

We'll migrate accounts in batches starting [date]. Yours is scheduled for [window], and you'll get a reminder a week ahead and again the morning of. Expect roughly [N] minutes of read-only access during the switch. If that window is bad for you, reply to this email and we'll move you to a different batch.

If something breaks afterward, write to [support address] and put MIGRATION in the subject line — those go to a dedicated queue through [date].

Full details, including the API changes and a rollback plan, are at [link].

— [Name], [Title]

---

Bracketed fields are yours to fill. Two spots worth real specifics: the *why now* line and the "[Feature X] works differently" bullet — vague versions of those are what generate support tickets.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.
